title: Split Array Largest Sum
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, split `nums` into `k` non-empty contiguous subarrays. Return the minimized largest sum of the split, i.e. minimize the maximum sum among the `k` subarrays over all possible ways to split.

examples.explanation: Splitting into [7,2,5] and [10,8] gives sums 14 and 18. This is the split that minimizes the largest sum.

hints: Trying every possible way to split the array into k contiguous parts is exponential — instead think about the answer itself, the maximum subarray sum, as the thing to search over.
The minimum possible answer is the largest single element (a subarray can't have a smaller max than its biggest element), and the maximum possible answer is the sum of the whole array (using k=1).

For a candidate maximum sum limit, greedily count how many subarrays are needed by adding elements to the current group until adding one more would exceed the limit, then starting a new group. That count is monotonically non-increasing as the limit grows, so binary search for the smallest limit that needs at most k groups.

solution.approach: Binary search on the answer: the minimized largest subarray sum. The search range is [max(nums), sum(nums)], since no valid split can have a max below the largest single element, and one group holding everything is always valid. For a candidate limit, greedily walk through nums, accumulating into the current subarray until adding the next element would exceed the limit, at which point start a new subarray; count how many subarrays this requires. This count is monotonically non-increasing as the limit increases, so binary search for the smallest limit requiring at most k subarrays, which is exactly the minimized largest sum.
